Before you engage the blade, lower the guard to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece. Check the tensioning wheel periodically throughout the shift, regardless of guard position. Tension can drift even when the machine has not run continuously.

Inspect the lower blade guide for wear whenever you change the blade. If the replacement blade matches the width and pitch of the original, a visual check is sufficient, provided you have completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual.

Do not wear loose clothing or jewelry near the machine. Tie back long hair.

Wait until the blade comes to a complete stop before you leave the work area. The machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes, so use caution even after the blade stops.
